title: Soyuz-TM

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: Soyuz is the Russian crew spacecraft, flown since 1967; the Soyuz-TM version flew from 1986 to 2002 to the Mir and International space stations. Three astronauts lie in body-shaped seats in the descent capsule; the commander in the middle faces the Neptun panel, with the rotation controller at the right hand and the translation controller at the left. Docking is normally automatic; the controllers are for a manual approach. The panel contents are summarised from public sources.

areas.name: Neptun control panel
areas.text: The main panel in front of the commander.

panels.name: Neptun control panel
panels.text: The main panel in front of the commander with screens, command keys, a navigation globe and clocks.
panels.context: Most of a Soyuz flight runs automatically; the crew watches it here and steps in when needed.

controls.name: Display screens
controls.text: Screens that show the state of the systems and the data of the approach to the space station.
controls.context: The commander watches the approach on them and takes over by hand if the automatic docking fails.

controls.name: Command keys
controls.text: Rows of keys that send commands to the spacecraft. The crew presses them with a pointer stick, because strapped into the seats they cannot reach the panel with their hands.
controls.context: The pointer stick is a simple, well-known Soyuz tool. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

controls.name: Globus navigation globe
controls.text: A small globe that turns to show where the spacecraft is over the Earth.
controls.context: It is an electro-mechanical instrument that gives the position without a computer screen.

controls.name: Clocks
controls.text: Clocks that show the time and count down to events.
controls.context: Engine burns and the return are timed to the second.

areas.name: Seats and sight
areas.text: The optical sight and the side seats.

panels.name: Periscope / optical sight (VSK)
panels.text: The viewing device used for the manual approach.
panels.context: It looks out of the spacecraft and shows the docking target or the Earth.

controls.name: Optical sight
controls.text: A periscope-like sight through which the commander sees the docking target on the space station.
controls.context: During a manual approach the commander keeps the target centred in it while steering with the two hand controllers.

panels.name: Left and right crew seats
panels.text: The seats of the flight engineer on the left and the third crew member on the right.
panels.context: Each seat is shaped to its astronaut's body to protect him during launch and landing.

controls.name: Side panels
controls.text: Each side seat has its own small panels with switches.
controls.context: JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

panels.name: Descent control handle
panels.text: A handle for steering the return by hand.
panels.context: It is for an emergency return when the automatic control does not work.

controls.name: Descent control handle
controls.text: This handle lets the commander control the lift of the descent capsule by hand during the return through the atmosphere.
controls.context: Normally the computer steers the return; JoyPro's catalog marks the details of this handle as uncertain.

panels.name: RUO orientation hand controller
panels.text: The handle at the commander's right hand.
panels.context: It turns the spacecraft; the same layout is used for the manual docking controls on the space station (TORU).

controls.name: RUO orientation hand controller
controls.text: Moving this handle turns the spacecraft: pitch, roll and yaw, by firing the small rocket jets around the spacecraft (thrusters).
controls.context: On a joystick it is the X, Y and twist axes; the commander uses it in a manual approach.

panels.name: RUD motion (translation) hand controller
panels.text: The handle at the commander's left hand.
panels.context: It moves the spacecraft without turning it.

controls.name: RUD motion (translation) hand controller
controls.text: This handle moves the whole spacecraft forward, back, left, right, up or down (translation), by firing the steering jets.
controls.context: In a manual docking the commander closes in on the station with it while keeping the target centred.
